summary: Parent-reported: the child has had pain in the right knee for about three weeks after twisting it during a football match. The swelling settled, but the pain returns with running and climbing stairs and she limps after school on some days. She rested for a week on the family doctor's advice and takes paracetamol syrup when the pain is bad. The parent reports a peanut allergy with hives. Everything here is parent-reported and needs to be checked at the visit.
reason_for_visit: Right knee pain after football practice for about three weeks.
history: Twisted the right knee during a match about three weeks ago. Swelling went down; pain comes back with running and stairs. Ice pack and one week of rest advised by the family doctor.
current_concerns: Pain when running or climbing stairs
Limps after school on some days
Worried she will stop playing sports

medications.name: Paracetamol syrup
medications.details: 5 ml when the pain is bad, about twice a week

questions_for_provider: When can she go back to football?
Which exercises can the family do at home?
Check knee stability and gait (limping after school reported).
